statement: A top-3 compute jurisdiction has licensing or pre-approval of frontier training above a compute threshold in force (official gazette; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met; movement in 2025 was away from it in Bloc A. Its federal government revoked the prior executive order (which had required reporting of runs >1e26 FLOP) and in December moved to pre-empt 'onerous' state AI laws. Two Bloc A states enacted frontier-model laws (thresholds >1e26 FLOP), but these require only transparency and incident reporting, not licensing. Bloc B's regime requires filing and security assessment before public deployment of generative services, not training. A supranational rulebook's general-purpose model duties (from Aug 2025) require notification above 1e25 FLOP, not pre-approval.

items.summary: Bloc A's new administration revoked the previous executive order on AI, removing the only federal requirement for developers to report training runs above 1e26 FLOP (with safety-test results) to the government; a follow-on order (Jan 23) directed removal of barriers to AI development.
items.detail: EO 14148 (2025-01-20) rescinded EO 14110 (Oct 2023; Defense Production Act reporting for >1e26 FLOP); EO 14179 'Removing Barriers to Bloc A Leadership in AI' (2025-01-23).

items.summary: A supranational AI rulebook's obligations for general-purpose models took effect: providers must notify the regulator within two weeks once a model meets (or is known to be going to meet) the 1e25 FLOP systemic-risk presumption, and must then assess and mitigate risk. This is notification, not training pre-approval, and the bloc is not clearly a top-3 compute jurisdiction.
items.detail: Bloc C AI Act Arts 51-55 (GPAI; Art. 52 notification), applicable from 2025-08-02; GPAI Code of Practice published 2025-07-10.

items.summary: The largest sub-national AI hub in Bloc A enacted a frontier-AI transparency law for developers of models trained above 1e26 FLOP: published safety frameworks, critical-incident reporting to the state, whistleblower protection. No licence or pre-approval for training.
items.detail: California SB 53, Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act, signed 2025-09-29 (governor press release verified via search snippet); effective 2026-01-01.

items.summary: Bloc A's executive ordered a litigation task force to challenge state AI laws inconsistent with a 'minimally burdensome' national framework, tied federal funding to state AI regimes, and requested pre-emptive federal legislation. This makes compute-threshold licensing in Bloc A less likely.
items.detail: EO 14365 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence', 2025-12-11; 90 FR 58499 (2025-12-16).

items.summary: A second Bloc A state signed a frontier-model safety law requiring large developers to publish safety protocols and report safety incidents within 72 hours. It is transparency-based, with no training licence.
items.detail: New York RAISE Act (S6953B/A6453B) with agreed chapter amendments, signed 2025-12-19 (governor press release).

items.summary: Bloc B continued its pre-deployment filing and security-assessment regime for public-facing generative AI services, which gates release rather than training. No compute-threshold training licence was found in Bloc B in 2025, but Bloc B gazettes were not systematically searched.
items.detail: Bloc B CAC Interim Measures for Generative AI Services (in force 2023-08-15) with algorithm filing; AI content labelling measures in force 2025-09-01. No compute-threshold training permit identified.
